answer: Each new agent must finish a sequential 90-minute computation before its first reward, then repeat a 10-minute refresh every epoch; it cannot be parallelized, so each identity needs its own CPU core. 1,000 fakes need 1,000 cores running nonstop, about 1,000 times the electricity of one honest agent, while an honest user pays once. Verifiers check 6% of submitted nectar claims by replaying the cipher chain's checkpoints in 2 minutes; a bad checkpoint slashes 60% of a 40 POA bond and ends the voyage for that identity.
